abstract: |
  We present a harmonized global dataset generated through the tricot (triadic comparisons of technology options) citizen science approach, comprising decentralized on-farm agricultural experiments conducted between 2011 and 2025 across more than 25 countries and over 30 crop species. The dataset represents the outcome of a long-term effort to develop a FAIR-by-design infrastructure for agricultural experimentation, integrating standardized protocols, digital data collection, controlled vocabularies, environmental covariates, socio-economic information, and links to external repositories. The resulting resource provides a unique foundation for studying farmer preferences, genotype-by-environment interactions, climate adaptation, technology adoption, and participatory breeding at unprecedented scale.

# Introduction

Agricultural innovation increasingly requires decentralized, context-specific evidence generated directly in the target environments \citep{deSousa2021, Atlin2001}. The tricot (triadic comparison of technology options) approach was developed to address this challenge by enabling large-scale citizen science experimentation in agriculture \citep{vanEtten2016, vanEtten2011}. Early implementations in Ethiopia, India, and Central America demonstrated that farmers could generate robust experimental data through simple, distributed trial designs \citep{vanEtten2016, vanEtten2019, deSousa2021, deSousa2024}.

Briefly summarize:

* Origins of tricot \citep{vanEtten2016, vanEtten2011}.
* First pilot studies \citep{vanEtten2019, deSousa2021, Moyo2021}
* Citizen science rationale \citep{Steinke2017, vandeGevel2020}.

# The tricot research infrastructure

Over the last fifteen years, tricot evolved from a participatory experimental method into a global digital FAIR-by-design infrastructure supporting decentralized agricultural experimentation.

Short description of the development phases, for example Phase I (2011–2016) where we tested tricot as proof of concept with pilot trials in Ethiopia, India, Central America \citep{vanEtten2016}, early digital tools \citep{vanEtten2016} and initial climate adaptation applications \citep{vanEtten2019}. 

Then Phase II (2017–2022) on the digitalization and scaling, with the new version of ClimMob \citep{Quiros2024}, expansion across countries, crops and contexts \cite{Brown2022, Donovan2025, Moyo2021, Nanyonjo2024, Olaosebikan2023}, and integration into breeding programs \citep{Daudi2026, Sharma2025, Kang2025, EmmanuelAlamu2023}.

Then finally to institutionalization and digital interoperability in Phase III (2022–Present), standardized metadata, ontology mapping, SOP development, and interoperability with external systems \citep{Selby2025}.

# The tricot open data community

The data insfrastuscture represents a collaborative effort involving CGIAR centers, national agricultural research systems, NGOs, universities, and farmer communities. The repository is intended as a living resource that will continue to expand through future contributions.
